q: What is Figure B that is a bracket used to hold and secure glass panels in place, often seen in glass railings and balustrades without full framing?
n: A glass clamp holds railing panels without a full frame.

q: What is Figure C that is a large exterior building system consisting of glass panels supported by a metal framework, creating a transparent facade?
n: A curtain wall hangs glass on a metal framework.

q: What is Figure D that is a fitting with multiple arms used to connect and support glass panels at point-fixings in frameless facade systems?
n: A spider fitting supports glass at point fixings.

q: What is Figure E that is a type of post support used to hold glass panels vertically in frameless glass balustrades or pool fencing?
n: A spigot is the post that holds frameless balustrade glass upright.

q: Which hardware can be specified for an entrance canopy?
n: Point-fixed spider fittings carry glass canopies.

q: Which hardware is structurally appropriate for laminated glass?
n: Point-fixed spider fittings (Figure A) need laminated (tempered) glass.

q: Which hardware can be specified for tempered glass?
n: All the fittings shown are made for tempered glass.

q: Which hardware can be specified for annealed glass?
n: None: drilled or clamped frameless fittings need tempered glass, not annealed.

q: Which hardware can be specified for a large glass wall?
n: Spider fittings (Figure A) carry large point-fixed glass walls.

q: Which of the following is used as a fitting for securing glass balustrades that include a continuous handrail for added safety and support?
n: Figure D is the slotted handrail cap that runs along the top of the glass.

q: Which of the following is used for installing lightweight glass panels in display cabinets, providing secure but minimal fittings?
n: Small glass clamps fix lightweight panels in display cabinets.

q: Which of the following is used in shower enclosures with sliding glass panels and providing smooth movement?
n: Figure B shows the roller connectors of a sliding shower panel.

q: Which of the following is used for mounting frameless glass balustrades, providing structural support without a handrail?
n: A floor spigot holds frameless balustrade glass without a handrail.

q: Which of the following is used in swing doors where glass panels are joined edge-to-edge, allowing a seamless look?
n: A glass-to-glass hinge joins swing-door panels edge to edge.

q: What glass has a metallic coating to reflect heat?
n: Reflective glass has a metal-oxide coating.

q: What is a hollow, translucent glass unit made by fusing two halves with a partial vacuum inside?
n: Glass blocks are two pressed halves sealed together.

q: Which glass has minimal distortion?
n: Float glass is flat and distortion-free; tempering adds slight roller wave.

q: Which glass lets you see the people inside at night when the lights are on?
n: Reflective glass mirrors the brighter side, so at night it shows the lit interior.

q: What type of glass is translucent during the day but acts like a mirror at night?
n: Per the MST answer key: Reflective glass.

q: What material is used for windows to block excessive sunlight?
n: Per the MST answer key: Solar tint.

q: Heat-absorbing glass in blue-green or gray cuts solar heat because of its:
n: Metal oxides in the batch absorb solar energy.

q: What gives double (insulating) glazing its thermal performance?
n: The sealed air space slows heat flow.

q: What does fire-resistive glass contain between its panels?
n: Gel-filled fire-resistive glass holds a water-based gel that absorbs heat.

q: Which material is NOT advisable to use on the south side for energy conservation?
o: Heavy tinted glass and thick concrete wall
Transparent glass and light metal panels
n: In the Philippines the south side gets the most sun; clear glass and thin metal panels admit the most heat.

q: What is the standard face size of a glass block?
n: The standard block is nominally 8" × 8" (about 200 mm).

q: What is the main purpose of glass blocks?
o: Admitting light while obscuring the view
n: Glass blocks give privacy with daylight.

q: Why do glass blocks insulate fairly well?
n: The sealed hollow core slows heat flow.

q: Where should glass blocks NOT be used?
n: Glass block is non-structural infill.

q: How are glass blocks installed?
o: Bedded in Portland cement mortar with steel rods in the joints, then sealed with clear silicone
Glued into a wooden frame with contact cement
Stacked like CHB with bars through the blocks
Stuck to concrete with grout and tile adhesive
n: They are laid in reinforced mortar joints.

q: Where is wired glass best used?
n: Wired glass holds together when broken, so it is used overhead in skylights.
